text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures closed stronger but below an all-time high of 101.48. Failure to break the level could leave Bunds stuck in ranges on Wednesday ahead of U.S. GDP data. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.28, up 0.12 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled just above day's lows after budget. But slightly diminished need for interest rate tightening, following fiscal forecasts, helps short sterling, analysts said. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-28/32, down 08/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures ignored the the negative impact of the truck drivers' strike on the French franc and followed Bunds and U.S. bond higher to settle within a whisker of the contract high reached last week. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.10 up 0.26 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures were knocked back at the close on selling pressure after a buoyant session on domestic political jitters over judicial problems of Prime Minister Romano Prodi and some retracement in Treasuries and Bunds, traders said. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.83 down 0.25 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were firm but off the day's highs in active midday trade as profit-taking set in after key technical levels were hit late in the morning session, analysts said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 115-23/32, up 08/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.40 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Tuesday's Tokyo session sharply higher after a better-than-expected 10-year JGB auction, traders said. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 125.25, up 0.65 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issues activity stepped up a gear but remained way behind the pace set in recent weeks. British supermarket firm J. Sainsbury set a $200 million bond via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell which reoffered the 6.25 percent issue 32 basis points over the November 2001 U.S. Treasury note, itself yielding just over 5.90 percent. However, the Sainsbury deal was a 5-1/4 year financing and the spread was several b.p. tighter to U.S. Treasury paper of comparable maturity, which yielded close to 6.00 percent.
